title: What If We Stored All Our Data in DNA?

scenes.text: What if we stored our data in DNA? One gram could hold 214 petabytes.
In 2017, researchers at Columbia University and the New York Genome Center reached 214 petabytes per gram.
That is over eight times denser than earlier DNA storage work, and theory says up to 455 exabytes per gram.
The team copied the data through nine rounds of copies, then still read it back perfectly.
DNA needs no cold storage and does not degrade the way other media do.
The catch: writing the data cost about 7,000 dollars and two weeks. For now, it is for archives, not phones.
